# ENTROPY_SRC Core Module Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The entropy source core module is the main processing block of the entropy source IP. It collects raw random bits from a physical random number generator interface, performs continuous health testing on those bits, optionally conditions them with a SHA3-based cryptographic conditioner, and delivers validated entropy seeds to either a hardware consumer or to firmware through a register interface.

The module also supports a firmware-override mode in which firmware can observe raw entropy data, perform its own health testing or conditioning, and inject data back into the entropy pipeline. The module is responsible for detecting and reporting fatal internal errors, health-test failures, configuration errors, and entropy path integrity violations.

## 2. General Functional Requirements

- The module must operate from a single clock and an asynchronous active-low reset.
- After reset, the module must be in a disabled state with no entropy sampling, no seed delivery, no interrupts asserted, and all internal counters and buffers cleared.
- The module must be configurable through its register interface. Writes to protected configuration fields must be ignored while register update locking is active.
- The module must provide status information back to software, including FIFO depths, health-test counters, high-water marks, error status, state machine status, and boot-phase status.
- The module must be able to buffer completed entropy seeds. The number of completed seeds that can be buffered is controlled by a design-time depth parameter.
- The module must use raw entropy samples of four bits per valid transfer. The final entropy seed size is 384 bits. The software read data width is 32 bits.

## 3. Enable and Configuration Behavior

The module must only begin entropy processing when the primary module enable is active. When the primary enable is deasserted:

- Raw entropy samples must not be accepted.
- Health tests must be disabled and their counters cleared.
- Internal data buffers must be cleared.
- No new conditioning operations may be started.
- Hardware entropy requests must not be acknowledged.
- Software entropy reads must not consume buffered entropy.

The module’s configuration fields use redundant multi-bit encodings. The module must treat a value that is neither a valid enabled nor disabled encoding as invalid. An invalid configuration field must not enable the associated feature, and the module must report it through a recovery alert status. This applies to:

- Primary module enable
- FIPS mode enable
- Entropy data register enable
- Firmware override mode, data insert, and SHA3 start controls
- Entropy routing and entropy type selection
- Single-bit sampling enable
- Threshold scope selection

The module must support a FIPS/normal mode and a bypass mode. The bypass mode is selected when FIPS mode is not enabled, or when the entropy routing and type configuration explicitly select a bypass software path. In bypass mode, the module must use bypass-specific health-test thresholds and windows, and must not tag the output seeds as FIPS compliant.

## 4. Random Source Interface

The module must provide an enable indication to the external random number source. When the module is disabled, the source must not be enabled by this module.

When enabled, the module must accept a four-bit raw entropy sample whenever the source indicates that the sample is valid. The module must ignore valid indications while disabled.

The module must also provide a FIPS-mode indication to the random source. This indication must be asserted when the module is operating in the FIPS/normal path and deasserted in bypass mode.

The module may optionally support single-bit sampling. When this feature is enabled:

- Exactly one bit from each four-bit raw sample is selected by a configuration field.
- The selected bits are packed into four-bit symbols for health testing and downstream processing.
- Seeds produced while single-bit sampling is enabled must not be marked as FIPS compliant.

## 5. Health Testing

The module must continuously test raw entropy samples before they are delivered as validated seeds. The health tests run on the selected entropy data and use the configured test windows.

The module must implement the following health tests:

- Repetition count test
- Repetition count symbol test
- Adaptive proportion test, with high and low threshold checks
- Bucket test
- Markov test, with high and low threshold checks
- External health-test interface

Each test must be individually enableable. The module must reset all health-test counters when the module is disabled, and when a health-test clear condition is asserted.

The repetition count tests must operate continuously on each entropy sample. They must not be restricted to the fixed window boundaries of the other tests.

The windowed tests must operate over a configured health-test window. Separate windows and thresholds must be available for FIPS mode and bypass mode. The module must select the FIPS or bypass window and thresholds based on the current operating mode.

At the end of each health-test window, the module must:

- Compare the measured values against the configured thresholds.
- Generate per-test failure pulses if a threshold is exceeded.
- Capture high-water-mark values for observability.
- Reset the windowed test counters for the next window.

The module must provide total failure counters for each test, as well as high-water-mark registers for both FIPS and bypass modes. A summary failure counter must count any health-test failure from any test.

If a health-test failure occurs while a seed is being accumulated, the module must not release that seed as a successfully validated seed. If the number of failures reaches the configured alert threshold, the module must generate a health-test-failed interrupt and a recovery alert.

### 5.1 External Health Test Interface

The module must expose an external health-test interface that carries the same entropy samples and validity indication used by the internal tests. The module must provide:

- The raw entropy bits under test
- A validity indication
- A clear signal for resetting external test counters
- An active signal to indicate when the external test should run
- High and low threshold values
- The health-test window value

The external health-test interface must return a test count and high/low failure pulses. The module must process these external results in the same way as internal health-test results, including updating high-water marks, total failure counters, and the summary failure counter.

## 6. Entropy Conditioning and Bypass Path

After health testing, the module must pack the raw entropy into larger words for efficient processing.

In FIPS/normal mode, the module must send the packed entropy through a SHA3-based conditioner. The conditioner must:

- Accept data only when it is ready.
- Generate a 384-bit conditioned entropy seed when complete.
- Provide backpressure so that no valid entropy is lost when the conditioner is busy.

In bypass mode, the module must not use the SHA3 conditioner. Instead, it must pack the post-health-test entropy directly into 384-bit blocks.

The module must select between the conditioned path and the bypass path based on the configured operating mode. The FIPS compliance tag on the final seed must only be asserted when the seed was generated through the FIPS condition path with full-width sampling and no bypass.

If the SHA3 conditioner reports an internal error, the module must report a fatal error and must not forward the affected seed as valid.

## 7. Firmware Override and Observe FIFO

The module must support a firmware override capability, but only when the corresponding OTP fuse enable is active. If the OTP enable is not active, firmware override controls must be ignored.

### 7.1 Observe Mode

When firmware override mode is active, the module must copy post-health-test entropy into an observe FIFO that firmware can read through the register interface.

The module must provide:

- The current depth of the observe FIFO.
- A programmable threshold for the observe FIFO.
- An interrupt when the observe FIFO depth reaches the programmed non-zero threshold.

The observe FIFO must not overwrite existing data. If a new entropy word arrives while the observe FIFO is full, the module must drop the new word and set an overflow status. After an overflow, the module must suppress further writes to the observe FIFO until the FIFO has been emptied, to preserve contiguity of the remaining data.

### 7.2 Entropy Insert Mode

The module must allow firmware to write entropy data back into the entropy pipeline. When entropy insert mode is active, data written by firmware must be accepted into the pre-conditioning buffer in place of the normal post-health-test stream.

The module must provide a write-full status. If firmware attempts to write while the pre-conditioning buffer is full, the write must be dropped and a recovery alert must be generated.

When firmware insert mode is used with the SHA3 conditioner, firmware must be able to start and stop the conditioner insertion operation through a hardware or register control. Deasserting the insert start control while the insertion buffer is still full must be reported as a recovery alert.

## 8. Final Entropy Buffer

The module must maintain a final entropy buffer for completed 384-bit seeds. Each buffer entry must also carry a FIPS-compliant flag.

The module must write a completed seed into the final buffer only when the buffer is not full. If the buffer is full, the producing path must be backpressured and no seed may be dropped.

The module must provide the current depth of the final buffer as status to software.

## 9. Seed Delivery

### 9.1 Hardware Entropy Output

When the entropy routing configuration selects the hardware path, the module must deliver seeds through a hardware entropy interface.

The module must present a 384-bit seed and its FIPS-compliant flag to the hardware consumer when a seed is available and a request is asserted. The module must acknowledge the request and remove the seed from the final buffer only when a seed is actually available. If the final buffer is empty, the module must not acknowledge the request.

### 9.2 Software Read Path

When the entropy routing configuration selects the software path, the module must transfer seeds from the final buffer into a software-readable word FIFO.

The module must generate an entropy-valid interrupt when the software word FIFO is non-empty and the module is enabled.

Software reads of the entropy data register must pop one 32-bit word from the software word FIFO. A full 384-bit seed requires twelve 32-bit reads.

The software read path must be functional only when both:

- The OTP fuse for firmware entropy reads is active.
- The entropy data register enable field is active.

If either condition is false, the entropy data register must read as zero and reads must not consume data from the software FIFO.

## 10. Entropy Path Integrity Monitoring

The module must monitor the entropy data path for repeated values in delivered seeds.

Each time a seed is delivered from the final buffer, the module must compare a portion of the seed with the corresponding portion of the previously delivered seed. If the compared portions are equal, the module must assert a recoverable bus-consistency alert.

This integrity check must not prevent the delivery of the seed, but it must inform software through the recovery alert status.

## 11. Halt Request Interface

The module must provide a halt request output and a halt acknowledge input.

The halt request must be asserted when the main entropy processing state machine determines that a conditioning operation should pause the downstream consumer to avoid correlated power activity. The module must hold the halt request asserted until the downstream consumer acknowledges it.

The halt request must be deasserted when the conditioning operation no longer requires the halt.

## 12. Interrupts

The module must generate the following interrupts:

- **Entropy valid**: Indicates that entropy data is available for software reads.
- **Health test failed**: Indicates that the health-test summary failure condition has triggered an alert.
- **Observe FIFO ready**: Indicates that the observe FIFO depth has reached the configured non-zero threshold.
- **Fatal error**: Indicates that a fatal internal error has been detected.

Each interrupt must be controlled through the standard interrupt enable, status, and test register fields.

## 13. Alerts and Error Reporting

### 13.1 Recovery Alerts

The module must generate a recovery alert for recoverable conditions, including:

- Invalid multi-bit configuration field encodings.
- Health-test alert threshold reached.
- Main processing state machine alert.
- Entropy bus consistency violation.
- Alert threshold configuration mismatch.
- Firmware override write to a full buffer.
- Firmware override shutdown with a still-full buffer.

The recovery alert output must pulse when any recovery alert condition becomes true. A test input must also be able to pulse the recovery alert output.

### 13.2 Fatal Alerts

The module must generate a fatal alert and a fatal-error interrupt when fatal internal errors are detected, including:

- FIFO protocol violations, such as writing to a full FIFO or reading from an empty FIFO.
- Internal state machine errors in the acknowledgement or main processing state machines.
- Internal counter consistency errors.
- SHA3 conditioner state or count errors.

The fatal alert output must be asserted while a fatal error condition is active. A test input must also be able to assert the fatal alert output.

### 13.3 Error Status Registers

The module must report error conditions in an error-code status register. The error status must distinguish the source of the error and the type of error.

FIFO errors must be reported both by which FIFO produced the error and by whether the error was a write error, a read error, or a state error.

The error status bits must remain set until cleared through the register interface.

## 14. Main Processing State Machine

The module must contain a main processing state machine that coordinates the overall flow of entropy from health testing through conditioning or bypass into the final buffer.

The state machine must:

- Wait until enough health-test entropy has been collected.
- Determine whether the current health-test window passed.
- Start the SHA3 conditioner when the FIPS path is selected.
- Move completed seeds into the final buffer.
- Provide a boot-phase-done status after the initial boot entropy generation phase has completed.
- Assert the halt request when required.
- Detect and report state machine errors.

The state machine must not allow a seed to be delivered if the current window has failed health testing. It must also not write to the final buffer when the final buffer is full.

## 15. Reset and Disable Behavior

On reset, the module must return to the fully disabled state.

When disabled by software:

- All active entropy processing must stop.
- Raw entropy from the random source must not be accepted.
- Health tests must stop and their counters clear.
- All internal data paths and FIFOs must clear.
- Software entropy reads must return zero and not consume data.
- Hardware entropy requests must not be acknowledged.
- Conditioning operations must stop.

After being disabled, the module must be able to be enabled again by software and resume normal entropy processing. The state machine and data paths must restart from a clean state.

# Behavioral Specification: Keccak Round Module

## 1. Overview

The module implements a parameterizable Keccak-f permutation engine for one Keccak state. It provides:

- A state storage element that can absorb message words.
- Execution of the full Keccak-f permutation, consisting of the required number of Keccak rounds.
- An optional two-share masked datapath for side-channel protection.
- A completion indication when the permutation has finished.
- Error status outputs for detected integrity failures.

This specification describes only the local behavior of the module. SHA3 padding, KMAC framing, and message formatting are outside the scope of this module.

## 2. Configuration

The module is compile-time configurable in the following ways:

- **State width**: The Keccak state width shall be one of the standard Keccak widths. The supported widths are derived from the Keccak specification.
- **Masking enable**: The module may be configured to operate in unmasked or first-order masked mode.
  - In unmasked mode, the state and message data use one share.
  - In masked mode, the state and message data use two shares, and the logical state is the XOR of the two shares.
- **Message word width**: Message words have a fixed width, nominally 64 bits. The state width must be divisible by the message word width.

The number of Keccak rounds executed for one full permutation is determined by the state width.

Let `Width` be the state width and `W = Width / 25`. The number of rounds is:

`rounds = 12 + 2 * log2(W)`

For a 1600-bit state, this is 24 rounds.

## 3. Reset Behavior

On reset:

- All internal state storage shall be cleared to zero.
- The control logic shall return to the idle state.
- The round counter shall be cleared.
- The ready output shall be asserted.
- The completion output shall be deasserted.
- All error status outputs shall be deasserted.

All state changes occur on the rising edge of the clock. The reset shall be asynchronous and active-low.

## 4. State Storage and Output

The module maintains a state of `Width` bits.

- In unmasked mode, the state is a single `Width`-bit vector.
- In masked mode, the state is held as two `Width`-bit shares. The logical state is the bitwise XOR of the two shares.

The state output shall reflect the current stored state at all times. This means:

- When a message word is absorbed, the state output reflects the updated state after the next clock edge.
- When a permutation is running, the state output reflects the current internal state, including intermediate round results.
- When the permutation completes, the state output holds the final permutation result.

The state is not automatically cleared after a permutation. It persists until it is overwritten, cleared, or reset.

The bit ordering shall be consistent with the Keccak specification. Bit 0 of the state corresponds to the first bit of the Keccak state array. Word-aligned slices are ordered from bit 0 upward.

## 5. Message Absorption

When the module is in the idle state, it shall accept message words.

A message word consists of:

- A valid indication.
- A word address selecting one word-aligned slice of the state.
- One or two shares of word data.

When a valid message word is received while idle:

- The addressed slice of the state shall be updated by XORing the incoming word into that slice.
- The other slices of the state shall remain unchanged.
- The module shall remain in the idle state.
- The ready output shall remain asserted, allowing subsequent message words to be accepted in consecutive cycles.

In masked mode, the XOR shall be performed share-by-share. Each message data share shall be XORed into the corresponding state share.

The address selects a word-aligned slice. For a state width of `Width` and a message word width of `DInWidth`, valid addresses are `0` to `(Width / DInWidth) - 1`. The selected slice occupies bits:

`addr * DInWidth` through `addr * DInWidth + DInWidth - 1`

A message word presented while the ready output is deasserted shall have no effect on the stored state.

## 6. Clearing the State

The module provides a clear request that zeros the stored state.

A clear operation shall be accepted only when the module is in the idle state and the clear request carries the defined valid encoding.

When a clear operation is accepted:

- All state shares shall be cleared to zero.
- The module shall remain idle.
- The ready output shall remain asserted.

A clear request presented outside idle or without a valid clear encoding shall not clear the stored state. Storage-reset integrity reporting is described in Section 10.3.

## 7. Keccak-f Permutation Execution

The module provides a run input that starts a complete Keccak-f permutation.

A run request shall be accepted only when the module is idle.

When a run request is accepted:

- The module shall begin executing the full Keccak-f permutation.
- The ready output shall be deasserted for the duration of the permutation.
- The run request does not need to remain asserted; the module shall continue through all rounds automatically.
- A run request presented while the module is not idle shall be ignored.

The module shall execute exactly the number of rounds required for the configured state width.

Each round shall implement the Keccak-f round function, including the Theta, Rho, Pi, Chi, and Iota steps, using the correct round constants for the current round index.

At the end of the final round:

- The state shall be updated to the final permutation result.
- The round counter shall be reset.
- The module shall return to the idle state.
- The completion output shall be asserted as a one-cycle pulse.
- The ready output shall be asserted again.

A new run may be started immediately after the completion pulse. A new permutation shall start from the current state, allowing repeated Keccak squeezing operations.

## 8. Masked Operation and Entropy Handling

When masking is enabled, the module shall preserve the two-share representation throughout the permutation. It shall not output an unmasked combined state.

Masked operation requires fresh random words for remasking. The random word width is half the state width.

The module shall:

- Request and consume entropy words at the points required by the masked Keccak datapath.
- Assert a consumption indication when it consumes an entropy word.
- Stall if the required entropy word is not available.
- Preserve the current state while stalled.
- Not advance to a masking-sensitive processing step using stale or invalid entropy.

The module may support a look-ahead random-ready indication. This indication allows the module to know, one cycle in advance, that a fresh entropy word will be available. The module may use this look-ahead to avoid unnecessary stalls.

The logical result of the permutation shall be independent of the particular entropy values. The entropy only affects the random share representation, not the logical state value.

When masking is disabled:

- The module does not require entropy.
- The random-data inputs shall be ignored.
- The consumption output shall not be asserted.

## 9. Completion Output

The completion output indicates that a full Keccak-f permutation has finished.

The completion output shall be a one-cycle pulse. When the completion pulse is asserted:

- The state output shall contain the final permutation result.
- The module shall be back in the idle state.
- The ready output shall be asserted.

The completion pulse is not asserted during normal message absorption or clearing.

## 10. Error Status Outputs

The module shall provide three error status outputs.

### 10.1 FSM Integrity Error

The module shall assert the FSM error output if the control logic is in an invalid encoding or has entered the terminal error state.

Once the terminal error state is entered, the module shall:

- Stop normal operation.
- Deassert the ready output.
- Ignore message and run requests.
- Remain in the terminal error state until reset.

### 10.2 Round Counter Integrity Error

The module shall assert the round-count error output when the internal round counter detects an integrity failure.

This output is an error status indication. It does not by itself change the normal completion behavior of the permutation.

### 10.3 Storage-Reset Integrity Error

The module shall assert the storage-reset error output when a storage reset is signaled under invalid conditions, such as when the module is not idle or when the clear request is not the valid true encoding.

## 11. Life-Cycle Escalation

The module has a life-cycle escalation input.

When life-cycle escalation is active:

- It shall override all other control behavior.
- The module shall transition to the terminal error state.
- Normal operation shall stop.
- The FSM error output shall be asserted.
- The module shall remain in the terminal error state until reset.

Life-cycle escalation shall take precedence over message absorption, clear operations, and run requests.

## 12. Assumptions and Constraints

The following constraints are assumed at the integration level:

- Message-word valid and run request should not be asserted in the same cycle. If both are asserted while idle, the message word is processed and the run request is ignored for that cycle.
- Message-word valid and run request are only meaningful while the module is idle.
- The clear request is expected to be asserted only while the module is idle.
- The message word address is expected to be valid whenever a message word is accepted.
- The state width must be compatible with the configured message word width.
- Masked operation requires that the state width is large enough for the masking datapath.

# KMAC/SHA3 Hardware Accelerator Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

This specification defines the required behavior of the KMAC/SHA3 hardware accelerator. The module implements:

- SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, and SHA3-512.
- SHAKE128 and SHAKE256 extendable-output functions.
- cSHAKE128 and cSHAKE256.
- KMAC authentication using 128-, 192-, 256-, 384-, or 512-bit secret keys.
- A hardware application interface that allows other blocks to request hashing operations.
- Security hardening using masked Keccak processing when configured at build time.

The module is controlled by software over a memory-mapped bus. It exposes a message-data window, a digest-state window, control and status registers, interrupts, entropy interfaces, key-management interfaces, and alert outputs.

## 2. Build-Time Modes

The module may be built in one of two mask-hardening configurations.

### 2.1 Masking Enabled

When masking is enabled:

- Secret key material and internal Keccak state must be represented as two shares.
- The module must use fresh entropy for Keccak round remasking.
- The module must request entropy from an entropy distribution network, or use software-provided seeds, according to software configuration.
- The digest state exposed to software must be produced as two shares, and software must combine the shares to obtain the unshared digest.
- A build-status output must indicate that masking is enabled.

### 2.2 Masking Disabled

When masking is disabled:

- The module must operate without entropy requests.
- The second share of the digest state must be zero.
- The second key-share input is not used.
- Entropy-related configuration and seed writes must be ignored.

### 2.3 Command Delay Option

The module may be built with a command delay feature for side-channel analysis. When this feature is enabled:

- Software commands may be buffered and presented to the processing engine after a fixed delay.
- At least one software command may be buffered while a previous command is still pending.
- A manual-run command, used to extend an output, must still be performed immediately when written by software.

### 2.4 Idle Policy Option

The module may be built with an option that permits the idle indication to be asserted while the message FIFO still contains data. This option is intended for side-channel analysis only. In the default configuration, the module is considered idle only when the hash engine is idle and the message FIFO is empty.

## 3. Interface and Observable Behavior

### 3.1 Bus Regions

The module provides a memory-mapped slave interface with:

- A control/status register region.
- A message-window region for software to push message data.
- A state-window region for software to read the current digest or Keccak state.

### 3.2 Control and Status

The module must expose configuration and status through its register interface.

Status information must include:

- Whether the hash engine is idle, absorbing, or squeezing.
- Whether the message FIFO is empty, full, and the current fill depth.
- Whether a fatal alert has occurred.
- Whether a recoverable control-update alert has occurred.
- Hash-count information used for entropy refresh logic.

### 3.3 Interrupts

The module must generate three interrupts:

1. **Hashing done interrupt**  
   This interrupt must be generated when a software-initiated hashing operation completes absorption and enters the output/squeeze phase. It must not be generated for hardware-initiated application operations; those operations report completion through their own response interface.

2. **Message FIFO empty interrupt**  
   This interrupt must be generated on the transition of the message FIFO from non-empty to empty.

3. **Error interrupt**  
   This interrupt must be generated when any error condition is reported to the error register.

All interrupts must support:

- Enable and disable.
- Software-triggered test.
- Pending-state observation.
- Software clearing.

### 3.4 Hardware Application Interfaces

The module may have multiple hardware application interfaces. These allow other hardware blocks to request hashing operations.

Behavior:

- If multiple application requests arrive at the same time, the module must select one using deterministic priority.
- A hardware request is initiated by the first valid data beat from the selected application.
- The module must process the request without requiring a software start command.
- For KMAC requests, the module must use the sideloaded secret-key interface and must not expose the key to software.
- For KMAC requests, the module must append the encoded output length automatically.
- When the hash operation completes, the module must return completion through the application response interface.
- A hardware-initiated operation must not generate the software “done” interrupt.

### 3.5 Idle Output

The module must provide a multi-bit idle output.

- After reset, the idle output must be asserted.
- The idle output must be asserted when the hash engine is idle and the message FIFO is empty.
- If the idle-policy build option is enabled, the idle output may be asserted even when the message FIFO is not empty.
- The idle output must be deasserted while a hashing operation is in progress.

### 3.6 Alert Outputs

The module must provide two alert outputs:

1. **Fatal fault alert**  
   This alert must be asserted when a fatal internal integrity fault is detected. Such faults include:
   - Invalid state-machine states.
   - Counter integrity errors.
   - Storage reset integrity errors.
   - Control storage integrity errors.
   - Bus integrity errors.
   - Life-cycle escalation.

   The fatal alert must remain asserted until reset.

2. **Recoverable operation alert**  
   This alert must be asserted when a recoverable control-update integrity error is detected. It may be cleared by software acknowledgment or by returning the module to an operable state.

The module must support software-triggered alert tests.

### 3.7 Life-Cycle Escalation

When a life-cycle escalation condition is asserted:

- The module must stop all normal hashing activity.
- The module must unconditionally move to a terminal error state.
- The terminal error state must be left only by reset.
- No command, message write, or configuration update may take effect in this state.

## 4. Functional Operation

### 4.1 Initialization and Configuration

After reset, the module must be idle, with no active hash operation, an empty message FIFO, and no valid digest state.

Software must configure the module while it is idle. Configuration includes:

- Hash mode: SHA3, SHAKE, cSHAKE, or KMAC.
- Security strength.
- KMAC enable.
- Message data endianness.
- Digest state endianness.
- cSHAKE prefix: encoded function-name and customization string.
- Secret key and key length, for KMAC.
- Entropy mode, refresh settings, seeds, and entropy-ready indication.
- Message-masking enable, if available.
- Sideloaded-key enable.
- Enable for unsupported mode/strength combinations.

Configuration and key writes must take effect only while the module is idle. Writes attempted during an active operation must not affect the active operation.

### 4.2 Software Command Model

The module must support the following command operations:

- **Start**  
  Begin a new hash, KMAC, or extendable-output operation. After Start is accepted, the module must leave idle and begin its internal preamble processing.

- **Process**  
  Indicate the end of message data. The module must apply the correct padding and complete the absorbing phase. For software-initiated operations, Process completion must lead to the output/squeeze state and generate the “done” interrupt.

- **Manual Run**  
  Execute one additional Keccak permutation so that additional output data can be produced during expandable-output operations. Manual Run must be performed immediately when written, even if the command-delay option is enabled.

- **Done**  
  Terminate the current operation. The module must clear the hash state, internal padding state, and return to idle. Done must not clear software key material or configuration.

- **Entropy refresh request**  
  Request an explicit entropy reseed when masking is enabled.

- **Hash count clear**  
  Clear the internal entropy refresh hash counter.

### 4.3 Software-Initiated SHA3/SHAKE Operation

The expected operation sequence is:

1. Check that the module is idle.
2. Configure mode, strength, endianness, and any required prefix.
3. Write the message data to the message window.
4. Issue Process.
5. Wait for the done interrupt, or poll status until the module is in the squeeze state.
6. Read the digest from the state window.
7. If more output bits are needed than the current state contains, issue Manual Run and read the next state block; repeat as needed.
8. Issue Done to finish.

The module must accept message data in arbitrary byte chunks. Message length is not written as a separate software field; the module determines the message boundary from Process.

### 4.4 Software-Initiated KMAC Operation

For KMAC:

1. Enable KMAC mode and configure cSHAKE mode.
2. Load the secret key and key length.
3. Write the prefix. The first six bytes of the prefix must be the encoded function-name for KMAC.
4. Issue Start.
5. Write the message data.
6. Append the encoded right-encoded output length to the message stream.
7. Issue Process.
8. Wait for the done interrupt.
9. Read the authentication digest.
10. Issue Done.

When KMAC is enabled, the module must prepend the encoded key block to the message before performing the hash. The module must not require software to compute this key block manually.

If the key is supplied through the sideloaded-key interface and is not valid when KMAC begins, the module must report an error and enter a terminal error state.

### 4.5 cSHAKE Prefix Handling

When the module is configured in cSHAKE mode, it must process the encoded function-name and customization string before processing the message. This prefix processing is part of the hashing operation and occurs after Start but before message absorption.

### 4.6 Hardware-Initiated Application Operation

When a hardware application requests a hash operation:

1. The module must select an application request.
2. The module must automatically apply the algorithm configuration associated with that application.
3. The module must not require software to issue Start, Process, or Done.
4. The module must push the application message data through the same processing path.
5. On completion, the module must return the digest through the application response interface.

While a hardware application operation is active:

- Software commands must be ignored.
- Software writes to the message window must be ignored.
- An error must be reported if software attempts either action.

The module may withhold the software-readable digest state during hardware-initiated operations to prevent exposure of key-derived values.

## 5. Data Formatting and Endianness

### 5.1 Message Data

The module must accept message data in 32-bit bus words, with byte qualifiers for sub-word writes.

The module must pack partial words to the internal datapath width, so software can write messages of arbitrary byte length with no alignment requirement.

Software can select message byte order:

- Little-endian: bytes are consumed in the order written.
- Big-endian: each 32-bit word is byte-swapped before entering the message stream.

The secret key and cSHAKE prefix are always little-endian.

### 5.2 Digest State

The state window must provide access to the Keccak state after a software-initiated operation has completed absorption.

The digest state must be zero or invalid while:

- The module is idle.
- The module is still absorbing.
- A hardware-initiated operation is active.

Software can select the byte order of the state window.

### 5.3 Masked Digest State

When masking is enabled:

- The digest state must be exposed as two shares.
- Software must read both shares and XOR them to recover the true digest.
- The state window must not expose secret key material.

When masking is disabled:

- Only one share is produced.
- The second share region must read as zero.

### 5.4 Message Masking

When masking is enabled and message masking is configured, the module must internally combine incoming message data with a pseudo-random mask before the data enters the Keccak datapath.

Message masking must not change the final digest. It is a side-channel protection feature.

## 6. Entropy Behavior

### 6.1 Masking Enabled

When masking is enabled, the module must have an entropy source, either from the entropy distribution network or from software-seeded pseudo-random generation.

The module must use entropy for:

- Remasking the Keccak round function.
- Generating message masks when message masking is enabled.

The module must support:

- Software-supplied entropy seeds.
- Periodic refresh of internal entropy state.
- Explicit refresh requested by software.
- A refresh threshold based on the number of hash operations.

The module must report an error if the configured entropy mode is not a valid mode when the module is asked to produce entropy.

The module must report an error if a request to the entropy distribution network is not answered within the configured wait time. After such a timeout, the module should continue using previously generated entropy to avoid permanently stalling an in-progress operation, and software must be able to recover the module by acknowledging the error.

### 6.2 Masking Disabled

When masking is disabled:

- The entropy request interface must be inactive.
- All entropy-related configuration and seed writes must be ignored.
- Internal random values used by the datapath must be tied off to a safe non-acting state.

## 7. Error Reporting and Recovery

### 7.1 Error Reporting Interface

The module must provide an error code, error information, and an error interrupt.

When an error occurs:

- The error interrupt must be asserted.
- The error code must be captured in the error report register.
- The module may continue operation, enter a wait state, or enter a terminal error state, depending on the error class.

If multiple errors occur at the same time, the module must report one error according to a fixed priority. The reported error information may include context such as the current application state or the received command.

### 7.2 Command and Configuration Errors

The module must report errors for:

- Software writes to the message FIFO when message input is not currently accepted.
- Software commands issued while a hardware application operation is active.
- Software command sequences that do not match the expected Start, Process, Run, Done flow.
- Mode and security-strength combinations that are not supported.
- KMAC mode where the configured prefix is not the correct encoded KMAC function-name.

For unsupported mode/strength combinations and incorrect KMAC prefix:

- The module must report the error.
- The operation may still proceed.
- The resulting digest may not be meaningful.

For invalid command sequences and software writes during application activity:

- The offending command or write must be dropped.
- The ongoing operation must not be affected.

### 7.3 Entropy Errors

The module must report errors for:

- A sideloaded key that is not valid when KMAC begins.
- An entropy configuration that is not acceptable.
- An entropy distribution network response timeout.

A sideloaded-key invalid error must be treated as terminal and requires a reset.

Entropy timeout and invalid-entropy-mode errors must be recoverable: software can acknowledge the error and return the module to an operable state.

### 7.4 Fatal Faults

The module must assert the fatal fault alert for:

- Sparse state-machine errors.
- Counter integrity failures.
- Storage reset failures.
- Shadowed-storage integrity errors.
- Bus integrity errors.
- Life-cycle escalation.

When a fatal fault is detected:

- The module must stop normal operation.
- The fatal alert must remain asserted until reset.
- Software acknowledgment must not clear the fatal alert.

### 7.5 Recoverable Control-Update Faults

The module must assert the recoverable alert when a shadowed control-register update integrity failure is detected.

The recoverable alert must remain observable until software acknowledges the error or a new operation is started.

## 8. Reset Behavior

When reset is asserted:

- All outputs must be in their reset state.
- The module must be idle.
- The message FIFO must be empty.
- No digest must be available.
- Interrupts must be deasserted.
- The idle output must be asserted.

After reset is deasserted, the module must be ready for software configuration and operation.

## 9. Security Behavior

The module must protect secret key material:

- Secret keys must not appear in the software-readable state window.
- Secret keys must not be included in normal status output.
- In masked builds, key shares must not be exposed through a single-channel observation point.
- During life-cycle escalation, all keyed and hashing activity must be halted.

The module must ensure that the digest state is exposed only after absorption is complete and only for software-initiated operations where exposure is intended.

# SHA3 Core Module Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The SHA3 core is the Keccak sponge engine used for SHA3, SHAKE, and cSHAKE hashing operations. It accepts message data, performs the required padding and Keccak permutations, and exposes the resulting Keccak state as the digest output.

The module supports:

- SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512
- SHAKE-128 and SHAKE-256
- cSHAKE-128 and cSHAKE-256
- Byte-granular message input
- Optional masked operation, in which message and state values are represented as two Boolean shares

The module is controlled by four commands:

- Start: begin a new hashing operation
- Process: finalize message absorption and apply the final padding
- Run: manually perform one additional Keccak permutation while squeezing
- Done: finish the operation and return to idle

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

After reset, the module shall be in the idle state.

In the idle state:

- The module shall not accept message data.
- No Keccak permutation shall be running.
- The state output shall be zero.
- State-valid and squeezing status shall be deasserted.
- Only the Start command shall be accepted.
- Process, Run, or Done commands issued in idle shall be ignored and reported as software-control errors.

## 3. Command Behavior

### 3.1 Start

The Start command shall initialize a new hashing operation.

The module shall accept Start only while in the idle state.

When Start is accepted:

- The module shall enter the absorbing phase.
- The selected mode and strength shall determine the padding and Keccak rate for the operation.
- If cSHAKE mode is selected, the module shall first process the encoded function-name and customization string as the cSHAKE prefix before accepting message data.
- The module shall not expose the Keccak state during this phase.

### 3.2 Process

The Process command shall indicate that all message data for the current operation has been supplied.

The module shall accept Process only while in the absorbing phase, and only if a Process operation is not already being processed.

When Process is accepted:

- The module shall append the mode-specific padding and domain-separation bits required by the selected algorithm.
- The final padded block shall be absorbed.
- No further message data shall be accepted for the current operation after Process has been accepted.

### 3.3 Run

The Run command shall be accepted only while the module is in the squeezing phase.

When Run is accepted:

- The module shall perform exactly one Keccak permutation on the current state.
- While that permutation is running, the state output shall be invalid and held to zero.
- When the permutation completes, the state output shall become valid again.
- The Run command may be repeated to generate additional squeezing output when the requested output length exceeds the Keccak rate.

### 3.4 Done

The Done command shall be accepted only while the module is in the squeezing phase.

When Done is accepted:

- The module shall terminate the current operation.
- The absorbing/squeezing status indicators shall be deasserted.
- The Keccak state shall be cleared.
- The state output shall return to zero.
- The module shall return to the idle state after a short internal flush transition.

## 4. Message Input and Absorption

The message input uses a valid/ready handshake. A message transfer occurs only when the module indicates that it is ready and the producer asserts valid data.

The module shall:

- Accept message bytes only after a Start command has been accepted.
- Use the byte strobes to determine which bytes in a transfer are valid.
- Ignore bytes that are not selected by the strobes.
- Apply the same byte strobes to all shares when masked operation is enabled.
- Accumulate message bytes into blocks of the size determined by the configured Keccak rate.
- Run a Keccak permutation each time a full rate block has been accumulated.
- Assert a block-complete indication each time a Keccak permutation completes.

The module shall not require the software to provide the message length. The Process command is used to mark the end of the message.

## 5. cSHAKE Prefix Handling

When cSHAKE mode is selected, the module shall use the supplied function-name and customization string to construct the cSHAKE prefix as defined by NIST SP 800-185.

The prefix shall be absorbed before any message data is accepted. The module shall generate and process the required padding for the prefix in accordance with the selected cSHAKE strength. Changing the function-name or customization string during an active operation shall not affect that operation.

## 6. Squeezing and State Output

The module shall expose the full 1600-bit Keccak state after the absorbing phase is complete.

The state output shall be valid only during the squeezing phase and only when a manual Run command is not actively executing. In all other states, including idle, absorption, manual-run, flush, and terminal error, the state output shall be forced to zero to prevent information leakage.

When masked operation is enabled, the state output shall be provided as two shares. When masking is disabled, a single share shall be provided.

An absorbed indication shall be asserted when the final padded block has been absorbed and the module is ready to enter the squeezing phase. A squeezing status shall be asserted while the module is in the squeezing phase and the state output is available for reading.

During the squeezing phase:

- The module shall keep the Keccak state stable until a Run or Done command is accepted.
- Accepting a Run command shall temporarily invalidate the state output while the permutation is in progress.
- Accepting a Done command shall clear the state and end the squeezing phase.

## 7. Entropy and Masking

When masked operation is enabled, the module shall consume random bits from the entropy interface during Keccak permutations. These random bits are required for remasking internal state shares.

If enough random data is not yet available, the module shall stall internal Keccak progress until the required random data is supplied. The module shall not produce incorrect state as a result of waiting.

The module shall indicate when it has accepted random data from the entropy interface.

When masking is disabled, the module shall not consume random data from the entropy interface.

## 8. Error Reporting

### 8.1 Software-Control Errors

The module shall report a software-control error when a command is issued that is not allowed in the current operating state. Examples include:

- Process, Run, or Done issued before Start
- Start issued while absorbing
- Process issued while a process operation is already in progress
- Run issued before absorption is complete
- Done issued before the squeezing phase is reached
- Run or Done issued during a manual-run operation

When such an illegal command is detected:

- The error shall be reported with a code indicating a software-control error.
- The error information shall indicate which command inputs were asserted.
- The illegal command shall be ignored for control purposes.
- The current operation shall continue unaffected.

### 8.2 FSM Error Reporting

The module shall assert an FSM error output if any internal controller enters an illegal state encoding. This includes the terminal error state reached on life-cycle escalation.

### 8.3 Counter Error Reporting

The module shall assert a counter error output if an internal round counter or message counter detects an unexpected condition during processing.

### 8.4 Keccak Storage Reset Error Reporting

The module shall assert the Keccak storage reset error output when the Keccak permutation engine reports an unauthorized storage reset.

## 9. Life-Cycle Escalation

When the life-cycle escalation input is asserted, the module shall unconditionally transition to the terminal error state from any current state.

In the terminal error state:

- Normal hashing operations shall stop.
- No commands shall be accepted.
- The state output shall be forced to zero.
- Absorbed and squeezing indicators shall be deasserted.
- The FSM error output shall be asserted.

The module shall remain in the terminal error state until reset.

## 10. Block-Progress and Observability Outputs

The module shall provide a block-complete output that pulses each time a Keccak permutation completes. This includes permutations performed for:

- cSHAKE prefix processing
- Absorbing message blocks
- The final padded block
- Software-triggered Run commands

The module shall also expose its current main controller state in encoded form for observability and debug purposes.
